description: These official statistics describe Scotland's single national fire and rescue service: where every fire station is, how it is crewed and equipped, and every fire it has attended since 2009-10. They are published by the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service as accredited official statistics, in two annual bulletins with downloadable workbooks. The fire stations dataset lists all 356 stations with coordinates, address, crewing model (wholetime, retained, volunteer or mixed), numbers of crews and pumps, specialist and national resilience capabilities, and the local authority, local senior officer area and service delivery area. A separate vehicles dataset covers the fleet, and the fires dataset gives incident-level fires from 2009-10 to 2024-25, alongside tables on casualties, non-fire incidents, false alarms and fire safety visits. All files are available as a free download in Excel format. Caveats: the incident file is large and needs the guidance notes, locations of incidents are generalised, and response times are reported in tables, not per incident. Simulation uses: building the station and appliance layer of fire service coverage and relocation models, testing station closures or crewing changes against historical demand, and calibrating wildfire and flood response scenarios. Related records: the US Fire Administration registry (data-usfa-national-fire-department-registry) and NFIRS (data-usfa-nfirs-public-data-release) are the US counterparts, and the Irish fire service statistics (data-ireland-fire-service-statistics-2016) a neighbouring example.
